title.narrative: Supporting the Elimination of PCB in the Electricity Sector and other Applications

description.narrative: Development of a global program to support the elimination of PCB from equipment in the electricity sector and other applications by leveraging transmission and distribution projects and other operations.

Global Environmental BenefitsThe project supports the compliance of Parties to the Stockholm Convention with PCB elimination deadlines. The elimination of PCB from equipment reduces the risk of toxic PCB leaking into the environment, global biota and the human food chain, which is a recognized GEB.Environmental and Social SafeguardsGiven that the MSP will focus on analytics, knowledge, and stakeholder consultations, no specific ESF-relevant risks have been identified. Risks associated with the implementation of child projects will be considered during child project preparation. For World Bank energy sector projects, these risks will be included in the ESF document of the underlaying operation, for which the MSP will develop a template, which will at least consider the following risks. ESF Risks Mitigation PCB spills to the environment during removal, transportation, and/or cleaning of PCB-containing equipment and containers. Child projects will use experienced contractors for this work. Personal protective equipment and other safety equipment to handle PCB and remove spills will be on hand. PCB in transit may be diverted or does not reach the destruction facility. PCB will be handled as hazardous waste. Child projects plans and executing agencies will make sure that the necessary permits (as required by the Basel Convention and national regulations) and safety measures are in place. PCB will be transported by companies duly authorized and equipped to handle hazardous waste. PCB destruction in incinerators and other authorized facilities may lead to contamination of environmental media. The MSP will support the selection of final disposal and destruction facilities, which will have to be duly licensed and equipped to handle and destroy hazardous waste including PCB. There may be power outages during removal and replacement of transformers and other equipment. Child projects agencies will work with equipment owners (utilities) to minimize negative impacts on power supply, chiefly through technical means.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
